title: Amazon White Background Photo Guide | AIVideosUGC
description: Make an Amazon white-background main image from a phone photo. Use pure white (RGB 255), fill 85% or more of the square, and add nothing extra.
h1: How to Make an Amazon White Background Photo for Your Main Image
lead: An Amazon white background photo is a square main image on pure white. The real product fills at least 85% of the square, and nothing extra is drawn on top.
summary: Make the main image pure white, and keep only what you ship. Fill most of the square, and check the result against the item in your hand.

sections.h2: What are the Amazon main image requirements?
paras: The main image needs a pure white background and the product you actually sell. Do not add text, badges (such as a sale sticker), or extra objects that do not come in the box.

Amazon's product image rules ask for pure white. That color is RGB 255, 255, 255, which means full white. The product should fill 85% or more of the square. Only the item being sold should appear. The same rules ask for a longest side of 500 pixels or more. A pixel is one tiny dot in the picture. Use 1,000 pixels or more if you want shoppers to zoom in. No side should be longer than 10,000 pixels. Clothing and jewelry listings can add more rules. Read the current Seller Central guide, Amazon's seller site, for your category before you upload.

True to the item. Compare shape, color, parts, and label with the product in your hand before you publish.

sections.h2: Does my phone photo already need a white background?
paras: No. It needs the whole product, in focus (sharp, not blurry), with even light and a little space around every edge.

Take the photo near a window, on a plain surface, and hold the phone at the product's height. Show what the buyer finds in the box. If two lids ship with the bottle, both lids belong in the photo. If a strap is sold separately, leave it out.

sections.h2: How do I make a pure white background product photo?
paras: Upload a clear photo of the whole product. Ask for that same item on pure white, including every piece that ships with it.

Open the [AI product background changer](page:change-background) or the [AI product photo generator](page:photo-hub). Then write one plain line, such as "the bottle and both lids on pure white." The old background comes off. The area behind the product is set to pure white. The result is square, which fits a main image. One image uses 24 credits. Credits are what you spend, and the cost is shown before you confirm. If the image does not finish, those credits come back. You can use the finished file in ads and on your store. No logo is stamped on the file.

sections.h2: The same white setup across the catalog
paras: A main image that breaks the white rule can be removed from the listing until you replace it. The listing can also stop showing in search.

Batch, many products at once, uses the same white background, the same crop, and the same size. The crop is how tight the product sits in the square. The API lets your own shop system start that work from the catalog you already keep. A new product then follows the same main-image setup. Each image is still 24 credits, shown before you confirm.
A brand kit keeps your colors, logo, and fonts in one place. Use it on later images and on new photos. Do not put lettering on the main image.

The main image stays pure white with only what you ship. [Photos of daily use](page:lifestyle-photos) and [photos with a person](page:model-photos) fill the later image spots. The brand kit can be used on those.

sections.h2: What Amazon product photo rules should I verify before upload?
paras: Check the corners with a color picker, a tool that reads the color of one spot. Then set the real product next to the screen and compare shape, color, parts, and label.

Each spot you check should be pure white, with no gray haze. Zoom in on labels, because small lettering is where a new image often goes wrong. If the words are wrong, try again from a sharper photo. Also check the size in the square. A tiny product in a wide white area looks small next to listings that fill the square.
sections.alt: Adult hands compare an olive canvas backpack with a blank white square card.

sections.h2: What if the product is white, clear, or a set?
paras: Set the item's shape first, light the edges, and show exactly how many pieces the listing sells.

A white product can disappear on white. Take the starting photo with light from one side, so the outline has soft shading. Mention gentle side light in the line you type. Clear glass shows the room behind it, so photograph it against a plain light wall. A three-pack should show three units, not two and not five. Puff up bags and soft items before the photo you start from, because the new image follows the shape it sees.
sections.alt: Adult hand shapes an olive canvas backpack upright on a white sweep.

sections.h2: Should a white background for product listings cover every image?
paras: No. Keep the white rules on the main image only. Use the later image spots to show the product in use, how big it is, and a close detail.

A useful set might show the bottle in a gym bag, a hand for size, and a close view of the lid seal. Make the pictures first, then add any words in your own editor. A soft shadow, if you want one, belongs on a later image, not on the pure-white main image. The same white main image can also be the first image on your own store, so shoppers see the same photo in both places. For scenes that are not the main image, [Photos of daily use](page:lifestyle-photos) are a separate file.

faq.q: Why does my white background look gray on Amazon?
faq.a: Part of the background is probably not fully white, often near a corner or under the product. Check a few spots. If they are off-white, make another version, or brighten the background in an editor before you upload.

faq.q: Can an AI-made photo be my Amazon main image?
faq.a: Yes, when it shows the product a buyer will receive. Match shape, color, parts, and label before you publish it. You can use the file in ads and on your store. No logo is stamped on the file. Category rules can change, so read the current Seller Central guide for your category before you upload.

faq.q: How do I verify the white before I upload?
faq.a: Confirm pure white at RGB 255, 255, 255 (full white), no extra objects, and the product filling at least 85% of the square.

faq.q: How many credits does one white image use?
faq.a: One image uses 24 credits. Credits are what you spend. The cost appears before you start. If it does not finish, the credits come back.
Compare the result with the real item. If the shape, color, or part count changed, do not upload that file. Run it again from a sharper photo.

faq.q: Which Amazon product photo rules sit outside the main image?
faq.a: Later images can show the product in use, how big it is, and a close detail. Keep prices and badges out of the picture and add those words yourself. Category rules for clothing and jewelry can be stricter, so check the current guide for your category.

faq.q: What if my Amazon main image breaks the rules?
faq.a: Replace it. A main image that breaks the white rule, the size rule, or the product rule can be removed from the listing. The listing can stop showing in search until the image is fixed. Later photos can show the product in use. Read the current Seller Central guide for your category before you upload again.

faq.q: What size should the Amazon file be?
faq.a: Amazon's published rules ask for a longest side of 500 pixels or more. A pixel is one tiny dot in the picture. Use 1,000 pixels or more if you want shoppers to zoom in. No side should be longer than 10,000 pixels. The picture should still show the real product.

faq.q: Can I use the same white background on many products?
faq.a: Yes. A batch applies the same background, the same crop (how tight the product sits), and the same size in one go. The API, your shop system, can start that from your catalog. One image is 24 credits, shown before you confirm.

faq.q: Can the API make the main image?
faq.a: Yes. The API, your own shop system, can use the same pure-white setup you use by hand. Include only what ships in the box.
